newsitem.title: POLAND: Bosch-Siemens to invest DM 35 mln in Polish plant.
newsitem.headline: Bosch-Siemens to invest DM 35 mln in Polish plant.

text.p: Germany's Bosch-Siemens Hausgeraete GmbH on Monday launched the construction of a state-of-the-art, 35-million-mark plant in Poland to produce 200,000 washing machines for central Europe.
"We will invest 35 million marks until April 1, 1997, when the production is due to start," Ronald Kuhlein, deputy president of Bosch-Siemens' washing machines and dryers department, told reporters.
"This will be Bosch-Siemens most state-of-the-art factory in the world," Kuhlein added.
He said production, amounting at first to 200,000 washing machines annually, could later expand to 400,000 units. If this happens, employment will be increased to 280 workers from 140 initially.

The factory, based in Poland's central city of Lodz, will export washing machines to other former Sovier bloc countries in central and eastern Europe. It will also become Bosch-Siemens' marketing centre for the region.
Bosch-Siemens is 50 percent owned by Siemens AG and 50 percent by Robert Bosch GmbH. It is the second biggest household appliances producer in Europe, with a 16-percent market share.
